slides.heading: Choose the week you can keep
slides.body: Start with reliable appointments, not the most demanding split.
slides.narration: The best workout split starts with a week you can actually keep. If Monday, Wednesday and Saturday are reliable but Friday often disappears, compare a three-day schedule before committing to four. This guide helps you organize the week. It does not prescribe your exercises, sets, effort or recovery.

slides.heading: Two or three reliable days
slides.body: Compare full-body sessions. Keep each exercise list manageable.
slides.narration: With two reliable visits, full-body sessions give you two places to include upper- and lower-body work. Three visits offer another appointment, but full body does not mean every exercise every time. A three-day upper and lower rotation is different: each half receives three dedicated sessions across two weeks, not two in every calendar week.

slides.heading: Four or five reliable days
slides.body: Upper/lower or a hybrid can divide planned work across more visits.
slides.narration: At four days, upper and lower sessions repeated twice provide a clear structure. At five, an upper, lower, push, pull and legs sequence is another example. Decide the weekly workload before dividing it. Adding days on top of an already full program is different from distributing the same planned work across shorter visits.

slides.heading: Six days is optional
slides.body: Push/pull/legs twice means six appointments, plus travel.
slides.narration: Six days can fit push, pull and legs twice. It is a larger attendance commitment, not a required destination. At forty-five minutes per visit, you reserve two hundred and seventy minutes for workouts alone. Four visits reserve one hundred and eighty. Also check Sunday next to Monday: the week does not reset your recovery.

slides.heading: What if Friday disappears?
slides.body: Four-day upper/lower: one upper visit lost. Three-day base: unchanged.
slides.narration: Compare Monday upper, Wednesday lower, Friday upper and Saturday lower with full body on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Lose Friday and the first plan has one upper and two lower visits left. The second retains its three scheduled visits. That is a calendar comparison, not evidence of equal training volume or better muscle growth. Session counts are not set counts.

slides.heading: The split name is not the result
slides.body: Research comparisons depend on equal training volume.
slides.narration: A twenty twenty-four review of fourteen studies and three hundred and ninety-two participants found no significant difference in measured strength and muscle growth between split and full-body routines when training volume was equated. That condition matters. It does not make two arbitrary programs equivalent or establish a universal winner for your life.
